vulnerability.title: Axios: Proxy-Authorization header leaks to redirect target when proxy is re-evaluated to direct connection
vulnerability.category_l2: stale Proxy-Authorization header retained when a redirect is re-evaluated to a direct connection and sent to the redirect target

fixed_releases.verified_content: Tag v1.16.0 peels to df53d7dd99b202fb194217abd127ae6a630e70dc; its lib/adapters/http.js blob 252c7d87 carries the isRedirect parameter and the case-insensitive Proxy-Authorization deletion block at lines 237-245 introduced by fix commit afca61a, so the released artifact contains the fix.

Tag v0.32.0 peels to 8db2d44896849a21ed9721185b1034df24e1ba7b; its lib/adapters/http.js blob 2e9f2b75 equals the post-backport blob of commit 2af6116 and contains removeProxyAuthorization(headers) at lines 40-44, called before proxy authorization is applied at lines 147 and 170.

vulnerability.vulnerable_commit_basis: tag v1.15.0 peels to 772a4e54, inside the advisory range >=1.0.0,<1.16.0; its lib/adapters/http.js blob b9981159 sets Proxy-Authorization in setProxy (line 219) and installs a beforeRedirects.proxy hook (lines 234-237) that re-invokes setProxy on redirect without deleting the stale header.

location.verification_method: Static read of lib/adapters/http.js at tag v1.15.0, the v1.16.0 release file, the fix commit afca61a and 0.x backport 2af6116 diffs against their parents, git object identity checks, and the saved OSV/CVE/NVD records. No JavaScript was executed and no request was made.

critical_operation.description: setProxy writes a Basic Proxy-Authorization header onto the request options whenever a credentialed proxy is selected (line 219), then installs a beforeRedirects.proxy hook that re-runs setProxy for the redirect target (lines 234-237). On the redirect re-invocation setProxy takes the !proxy branch when the target resolves to no proxy, does not add a new proxy, and never removes the header already copied onto redirectOptions; the stale credential is therefore sent to the redirect target. The v1 fix adds an isRedirect argument and deletes every case variant of Proxy-Authorization before re-applying proxy settings.

entry_point.description: The initial Node.js request calls setProxy(options, config.proxy, ...) at lines 668-672, which may attach Proxy-Authorization from an authenticated proxy; the request is later dispatched through follow-redirects at line 692 when maxRedirects is non-zero, so the beforeRedirects.proxy hook is reachable on every redirect.

authenticated proxy credentials are base64-encoded into options.headers['Proxy-Authorization']

source_crosscheck.notes: Every published severity is HIGH 7.5 and every record gives the same CVSS 3.1 vector, so severity is consistent. CWE sets differ only by refinement: the CNA and OSV list CWE-200, while Red Hat's NVD contribution adds CWE-201; there is no contradictory CWE. The affected ranges agree across the CNA, OSV and NVD affected data (>=1.0.0,<1.16.0 and <0.32.0), and v1.15.0 is inside the v1 range. Source independence is weak: the GHSA is the upstream project's advisory, the CNA is GitHub (the same organization that publishes the GHSA database entry), NVD has no independently authored metric and carries GitHub's and Red Hat's secondary metrics, and no third-party reproduction or exploit analysis was found; CISA-ADP and Red Hat add SSVC/product data rather than independent root-cause analysis. The fix and release facts rest on git object identity and package-file equality, not on advisory prose.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read lib/adapters/http.js at v1.15.0 and confirm that setProxy sets Proxy-Authorization only when a credentialed proxy is selected and that the beforeRedirects.proxy hook re-invokes it without clearing the header, so a redirect resolved to no proxy keeps the stale value.
An independent reviewer must confirm that v1.15.0 is inside the advisory range and is the exact tag commit 772a4e54, and that the file judged is the snapshot file (blob b9981159).

An independent reviewer must verify the v1 fix afca61a and the 0.x backport 2af6116 from the git objects, including that v1.16.0 and v0.32.0 are the fixed releases and their package artifacts contain the respective fixes.

An independent reviewer must decide whether the evidence is independent of the primary advisory source; the dossier records independent_of_primary=false because the GHSA, CNA and NVD metrics all trace to GitHub, so evidence_independent may fail and keep the entry below promotion.
An independent reviewer must check the affected range at both the v1 and 0.x lines and confirm that no earlier fixed release exists in the range.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No JavaScript was executed and no HTTP request was made: the stale-header path is read from setProxy and the fix tests, not reproduced against a live proxy.

Exploitation requires the application to use an authenticated proxy for the initial request and to follow redirects automatically to a target that resolves to no proxy (for example an https URL with HTTPS_PROXY unset); requests with maxRedirects 0 and browser adapters are unaffected.

The 0.x line was verified only at the backport commit and v0.32.0 release; no 0.31.x snapshot was analysed, so the lower end of that range rests on the advisory, while the v1 range is verified from source.
The shallow git fetches prevent merge-base ancestry checks; v1.15.0 predates the fix commit by date and both objects were read by exact SHA.
The NVD record has no NVD-authored CVSS or npm CPE mapping, so severity and product mapping rest on GitHub/Red Hat secondary data.
The backport commit mixes the fix with unrelated 0.32.0 changes; only the Proxy-Authorization hunks were treated as evidence.
open_questions: Whether follow-redirects copies the prior request headers into redirectOptions in all supported versions, which is what carries the stale header; the fix tests assume it and the advisory describes that path.
Whether the 0.x branch had an earlier partial fix between 0 and 0.32.0 that would narrow the affected range, which was not checked because no 0.x snapshot is in scope.
Whether any independent third party reproduced or analysed the flaw; none was found, so evidence independence is expected to fail unless the reviewer finds one.
